title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'équation des lacets' manuscript Grothendieck studies the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type equations (two-cycle, three-cycle (64)/(78), and (68)) for an element ξ, the image of f ∈ \hat F_2 = \hat\Pi_{0,3}. Section (VIII) pushes these equations into the 'congruence' quotient \hat\Pi_{0,3} → \hat\Gamma'(2) ⊂ SL(2,\hat Z), and then into SL(2,\hat Z)' = SL/±1. There the generators x, y become unipotent matrices l_0, l_1 (for example l_0 = (1 2; 0 1)). The automorphism σ_∞ acts by conjugation by the matrix S = (0 -1; 1 0).

Step 1, formula (90). He computes S g S^{-1} = (d -c; -b a). For g ∈ SL_2 this is ^t(g^{-1}), the contragredient. In the margin NB he notes that for g ∈ GL(2,A), A any commutative ring, the same matrix equals det(g)·^t(g^{-1}). He also notes that S^{-1} = -S, so S^2 = -1 ≠ 1 in SL(2,\hat Z). Thus S itself is not an involution, but conjugation by S is the involution g ↦ ^t g^{-1}, the Cartan-type involution.

Step 2, formula (91). Hence σ(g^{-1}) = ^t g and the commutator [σ_∞, g^{-1}] = S g^{-1} S^{-1} g = ^t g·g. The coboundary is g^{-1}σ(g) = g^{-1}·^t g^{-1} = (^t g·g)^{-1}, a symmetric unimodular matrix.

Step 3, cocycles. For h_0 ∈ SL(2,\hat Z), h_0σ(h_0) = h_0·^t h_0^{-1}. So the 1-cocycle condition for the Z/2 generated by σ_∞, h_0σ_∞(h_0) = 1, is equivalent to h_0 = ^t h_0 (statement (*)).

Step 4. He sets ξ = (A B; C D) and rewrites equation (68), σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ, as a cocycle condition (*) for h_0 = l_0^{-γ}ξ. On the next page:
- (92) gives h_0 = (A+2γC, B+2γD; C, D).
- Symmetry gives B + 2γD = C.
- Combined with C − B = 1 − D, which comes from the ρ-equation on the previous page, this yields (2γ+1)D = 1, i.e. ρD = 1, where ρ = 2γ+1 is the GT parameter λ.
- In the ±1 quotient, h_0 = −^t h_0 is excluded because D ≡ 1 mod 2.

Purpose. The whole computation determines the image in SL(2,\hat Z) of solutions of the GT/loop equations, i.e. how the congruence quotient constrains (λ, f).

Interpretation. The cohomological content is that twisted 1-cocycles for g ↦ ^t g^{-1} are symmetric matrices and coboundaries are the forms ^t g g. So H^1 classifies unimodular symmetric (binary quadratic) forms up to equivalence, which is classical.
errors: Transposition slip in (90): ^t g·g = (a²+c², ab+cd; ab+cd, b²+d²), not (a²+b², ac+bd; ac+bd, c²+d²); the latter is g·^t g.

Consequently the explicit matrix in (91) is wrong: g^{-1}σ_∞(g) = (^t g g)^{-1} = (b²+d², −(ab+cd); −(ab+cd), a²+c²). The written matrix equals σ_∞(g)g^{-1} = (g ^t g)^{-1}. The structural statement (91) = (^t g·g)^{-1} is correct, and the slip does not affect the later use (*) or (92)-(93).

The interlinear gloss 'σ_∞ g^{-1} σ_∞ g' omits an inverse on the second σ_∞. This is harmless only up to sign (σ_∞^{-1} = −σ_∞), i.e. in SL(2,\hat Z)' = SL/±1, which is indeed where the next page works.
Equation label (91) appears to be used twice (for g^{-1}σ_∞(g) and for ξ); the next page continues at (92).

ideas.what: Conjugation by S = (0 -1; 1 0) in SL_2 is the contragredient g ↦ ^t g^{-1}; on GL_2 it is det(g)·^t g^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Cartan involution / contragredient on SL_2 realized as an inner automorphism

ideas.what: Z/2-cocycles for the involution g ↦ ^t g^{-1} are the symmetric matrices, and coboundaries are (^t g g)^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian H^1(Z/2, SL_2) for the twisted action ↔ classes of unimodular symmetric forms

ideas.what: Reduction of the GT loop equation (68) in the congruence quotient SL(2,\hat Z)' to a symmetry condition on h_0 = l_0^{-γ}ξ, leading (next page) to ρD = 1 with ρ = 2γ+1 = λ.
ideas.modern_name: image of GT (or of G_Q via f_σ) in the congruence completion \hat Γ(2) ⊂ SL_2(\hat Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura and others on the action of GT/G_Q on congruence and elliptic quotients
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) treats the related Teichmüller tower and SL_2 material, but not this computation as far as known

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames the σ_∞-part of the loop/GT equations, projected to SL(2,\hat Z), as a nonabelian Z/2-cocycle problem whose solutions are symmetric matrices, i.e. quadratic forms. This is a cohomological reading of the 2-cycle-type relation in the congruence quotient. The result is consistent with the known fact that the Galois/GT action on the congruence quotient is essentially governed by λ (the cyclotomic character). The cocycle/quadratic-form viewpoint is a small, apparently unpublished presentational detail rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: (VIII) - Calculs dans Sl(2,\hat Z) : cocycles sous σ_∞ ... h_0σ_∞(h_0) = 1 ⟺ h_0 = ^t h_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck independently computed the congruence-quotient image of solutions of the GT equations, now known in the literature through work of Ihara and Lochak–Schneps. It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary matrix computations, including a transposition slip, used to reduce GT-type equations in the congruence quotient SL(2,\hat Z). The goal of determining the SL_2 image in terms of λ is consistent with known results; only the cocycle framing is a mildly interesting unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'Reprenons un g ∈ (a b; c d)' should read 'g = (a b; c d) ∈ Sl(2,\hat Z)'.
Margin NB: '(A = Ze)' is probably '(p.ex. A = Z_ℓ)' or similar; illegible, but the formula σ_∞gσ_∞^{-1} = (d −c; −b a) = (det g)·^t(g^{-1}) is clear.
Margin NB first line: 'σ_∞^{-1} = (0 1; −1 0) = −σ_∞' and 'σ_∞² ≠ 1 dans Sl(2,\hat Z)!' (the transcription has 'σ_∞^{-1} ≠ ±1').
The crossed-out attempt is 'h_0 = (· s; t u)', with the replacement 'h_0 ∈ Sl(2,\hat Z)'.
Last lines: 'qui équivaut aussi à (*), avec h_0 donné par (65)/(44)'. The struck line contains an attempted formula h_0 = l_0^{-γ}ξ ... 'pour l_0, l_1 ...'.
